exposure: Induced method (ovulation induction, IVF, or ICSI)
cohort: 180 induced twin pregnancies and 698 spontaneously conceived twin pregnancies delivered over 16 years at a tertiary obstetric center
finding: Induced twin pregnancies had higher rates of first-trimester bleeding, gestational diabetes, and discordant growth, but did not have significantly different neonatal outcomes or rates of prematurity, low birth weight, or other major perinatal complications compared to spontaneously conceived twin pregnancies.
mod_finding: IVF was a predictor for first-trimester bleeding, and both IVF and ICSI were predictors for cesarean section.
